reflection.text:
Unblinded truth was latrunculin B, an actin disruptor, while I concluded Microtubule stabilizers at p=0.88. I was driven by extreme tubulin readouts at 3-30 uM — tub_glcm_contrast z=+61.6 to +171.3 and tub_mean z=+33.5 to +57.9 (e2,e5,e6) — plus monotonic tub_mean dose-response rho=+1.00 (e9) and atlas 7/10 stabilizer neighbors at sim 0.83-0.92 (e8).

Those measurements misled because I had no actin channel and interpreted increased tubulin intensity/texture as bundles/stabilization. The atlas comparison reinforced the error because it returned no actin-disruptor class, only stabilizers, protein degradation and cholesterol-lowering, so similarity was meaningless for the true class. I also over-weighted e6 frac_mitotic_like z=+36.8 and discounted the flat dose trend rho=+0.20 p=0.8 (e10), and I treated the microscopist ambiguity between destabilizers vs stabilizers (e7) as residual noise rather than a clue of cell rounding/retraction from actin loss.

Acquisition choices made this worse: I sampled only 1, 3, 10, 30 uM rep 1 and chased the high-dose tubulin burst instead of low-dose actin phenotypes, nuclear dysmorphology at 1 uM (nuc_solidity z=-18.3, nuc_form_factor z=-12.3 in e3), and a direct F-actin readout that would have separated actin collapse with compensatory tubulin condensation from true stabilization (PMID 41208085).
what_was_right: Detected potent dose-dependent cytoskeletal toxicity with lower density and nuclear irregularity, including nuc_solidity z=-18.3 and nuc_area z=-10.4 at 1 uM (e3).
Recorded flat frac_mitotic_like dose-response rho=+0.20 p=0.8 (e10), which correctly argued against sustained mitotic arrest expected for a stabilizer.
Microscopist note of ambiguity and lower density (e7) correctly signaled the phenotype did not cleanly match canonical stabilizer bundles.
what_was_wrong: Misread massive tub_mean and tub_glcm_contrast increases at 3-30 uM (e2,e5,e6) plus rho=+1.00 (e9) as microtubule stabilization without testing actin loss or tubulin condensation from cell shrinkage.
Over-relied on compare_to_reference_atlas 7/10 stabilizers (e8) when the atlas offered no actin-disruptor alternative, making the vote circular.
Discounted e3 nuclear shape defects and e10 flat mitotic trend and did not acquire F-actin, low-dose, or replicate wells that could have revealed primary actin depolymerization.

citations.claim: Latrunculin B drives actin depolymerization, which defines its true mechanism as an actin disruptor rather than a microtubule stabilizer (PMID 41208085).

Actin depolymerization alone can remodel cell shape and trigger downstream phospho-signaling, explaining secondary tubulin-intensity and nuclear-shape changes without direct microtubule stabilization (PMID 15030313).

reflection.next_experiment: Co-stain the same dose range for F-actin (phalloidin) plus tubulin and DNA, with cell-area/contractility quantification and an in vitro actin-sequestration assay to test direct actin loss versus tubulin polymerization.

**Question.** Which mechanism-of-action class explains this compound's phenotype in MCF-7 cells?

## Experiments (4 of 6 wells)

## Hypothesis history

- after step 4: Microtubule stabilizers 0.55, Eg5 inhibitors 0.15, Microtubule destabilizers 0.10, Aurora kinase inhibitors 0.10, DNA damage 0.05, DNA replication 0.05
- after step 11: Microtubule stabilizers 0.88, Microtubule destabilizers 0.05, Eg5 inhibitors 0.03, Protein degradation 0.02, Aurora kinase inhibitors 0.02

## Conclusion

**Microtubule stabilizers** (stated probability 0.88); key evidence e2, e5, e6, e7, e8, e9.

Why: Monotonic tub increase, mitotic arrest visuals, 7/10 stabilizer neighbours.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: Live-cell SiR-tubulin imaging to show bundle formation/persistence plus in vitro tubulin polymerization assay.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Top MoA Microtubule stabilizers is well-supported: tub_mean z=+33 to +58 and tub_glcm_contrast z=+62 to +171 at 3-30 µM (e2,e5,e6), monotonic tub_mean dose-response rho=+1.00 (e9), and atlas 7/10 stabilizer neighbours at sim 0.83-0.92 (e8). Destabilizers/Eg5 (runner-ups) would not explain this massive tubulin increase plus atlas profile; phenotype ambiguity (e7) is appropriately accounted for by p=0.88 rather than higher.

## Unblinding

Compound: **latrunculin B** (PubChem CID [6436219](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/6436219))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: agent said **Microtubule stabilizers**, BBBC021 annotates **Actin disruptors**.

## Reflection

Unblinded truth was latrunculin B, an actin disruptor, while I concluded Microtubule stabilizers at p=0.88. I was driven by extreme tubulin readouts at 3-30 uM — tub_glcm_contrast z=+61.6 to +171.3 and tub_mean z=+33.5 to +57.9 (e2,e5,e6) — plus monotonic tub_mean dose-response rho=+1.00 (e9) and atlas 7/10 stabilizer neighbors at sim 0.83-0.92 (e8).

Those measurements misled because I had no actin channel and interpreted increased tubulin intensity/texture as bundles/stabilization. The atlas comparison reinforced the error because it returned no actin-disruptor class, only stabilizers, protein degradation and cholesterol-lowering, so similarity was meaningless for the true class. I also over-weighted e6 frac_mitotic_like z=+36.8 and discounted the flat dose trend rho=+0.20 p=0.8 (e10), and I treated the microscopist ambiguity between destabilizers vs stabilizers (e7) as residual noise rather than a clue of cell rounding/retraction from actin loss.

Acquisition choices made this worse: I sampled only 1, 3, 10, 30 uM rep 1 and chased the high-dose tubulin burst instead of low-dose actin phenotypes, nuclear dysmorphology at 1 uM (nuc_solidity z=-18.3, nuc_form_factor z=-12.3 in e3), and a direct F-actin readout that would have separated actin collapse with compensatory tubulin condensation from true stabilization (PMID 41208085).

What was right:
- Detected potent dose-dependent cytoskeletal toxicity with lower density and nuclear irregularity, including nuc_solidity z=-18.3 and nuc_area z=-10.4 at 1 uM (e3).
- Recorded flat frac_mitotic_like dose-response rho=+0.20 p=0.8 (e10), which correctly argued against sustained mitotic arrest expected for a stabilizer.
- Microscopist note of ambiguity and lower density (e7) correctly signaled the phenotype did not cleanly match canonical stabilizer bundles.

What was wrong or missed:
- Misread massive tub_mean and tub_glcm_contrast increases at 3-30 uM (e2,e5,e6) plus rho=+1.00 (e9) as microtubule stabilization without testing actin loss or tubulin condensation from cell shrinkage.
- Over-relied on compare_to_reference_atlas 7/10 stabilizers (e8) when the atlas offered no actin-disruptor alternative, making the vote circular.
- Discounted e3 nuclear shape defects and e10 flat mitotic trend and did not acquire F-actin, low-dose, or replicate wells that could have revealed primary actin depolymerization.

Proposed next experiment: Co-stain the same dose range for F-actin (phalloidin) plus tubulin and DNA, with cell-area/contractility quantification and an in vitro actin-sequestration assay to test direct actin loss versus tubulin polymerization.

## Citations

Citations verified: 2/2

- PMID [41208085](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41208085/): Actin depolymerization by Latrunculin B can either suppress or promote root gravitropism, depending on the developmental stages in Arabidopsis. *Plant Signal Behav* (2025) — Latrunculin B drives actin depolymerization, which defines its true mechanism as an actin disruptor rather than a microtubule stabilizer (PMID 41208085).
- PMID [15030313](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15030313/): Actin depolymerization-induced tyrosine phosphorylation of cortactin: the role of Fer kinase. *Biochem J* (2004) — Actin depolymerization alone can remodel cell shape and trigger downstream phospho-signaling, explaining secondary tubulin-intensity and nuclear-shape changes without direct microtubule stabilization (PMID 15030313).
